To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

naphthalene additions to estuarine microcosms caused significant changes to the bacterial community composition, and that these changes may be important to understanding the biogeochemical cycling of organic matter in estuaries.

1) the addition of napolthalene increased rates of napolthaline mineralization, bacterial production, and bacterial community composition; and 2) the bacterial community in the polycyclic aromatic hydorcarbon-amended treatment was different from the communities in glucose-amended and no-addition controls.

naphthalene additions to the bottom boundary layer (BBL) of the Delaware estuary caused changes in the composition of the BBL bacterial community, with some of the changes being similar to those caused by the addition of glucose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of naphthol and naphthalenes on microbial communities in estuarine environments.
the effects of anthropogenic inputs of polycyclic aromatic compounds (PAC) on the structure and function of the microbial communities in estuarine sediments and the water column.
the fate of organic compounds in estuaries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PAHs can have a significant impact on the bacterial community structure in estuarine waters and that this impact can be detected by DGGE and FIS

the microbial community in the natal estuary was significantly affected by the addition of natalene and the community structure was different from the community structure in the glucose amended and control treatments.
the addition of napolthlene to a natural bacterial community resulted in a change in community composition and a change in the rate of naphthaline mineralization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
naphthalene has a strong effect on the bacterial communities and the bacterial communities have a strong effect on naphthalene biodegradation.
the bacterial community in the Delaware estuaries is highly responsive to changes in the chemical composition of the water.
the addition of natalene to the microcosms resulted in increased rates of naphthaline biodegradation and bacterial production, as compared to the no-addition controls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
naphthalene can have significant effects on microbial community composition and structure.
naphthalene can have a significant impact on microbial community structure.
naphthalene can have large effects on bacterial communities and biogeochemical cycling.
